## Overview

Once a workload runs cleanly on `MockSlurmBackend`, moving to a university or cloud SLURM cluster requires two more pieces:

1. **Reproducible HPC Packaging:** Compiling C++, `CmdStan`, `RTMB`, `JAGS`, or geospatial libraries inside an Apptainer/Singularity container and generating a POSIX-safe `sbatch` array script.
2. **Production Orchestration & Interactive Offload:** Submitting over SSH via `SlurmSshBackend` (without requiring ZeroMQ ports) and exposing long-running jobs cleanly inside non-blocking `bslib`/Shiny apps.

## 1. Scanning Project Dependencies & Compiled Toolchains

`scan_project_env()` inspects `renv.lock`, `DESCRIPTION`, and R/Quarto source files to identify required packages, compiled toolchains, and Debian/Ubuntu system libraries:

```{r scan-env}
library(slurmpilot)

# Simulate a realistic statistical modeling project directory
proj_dir <- tempfile("sp_proj_")
dir.create(file.path(proj_dir, "R"), recursive = TRUE)

writeLines(c(
  "Package: hierarchicalstudy",
  "Version: 0.1.0",
  "Imports: lme4, Rcpp, RTMB, dplyr"
), file.path(proj_dir, "DESCRIPTION"))

writeLines(c(
  "library(cmdstanr)",
  "library(ggplot2)",
  "x <- tibble::tibble(a = 1:3)"
), file.path(proj_dir, "R", "fit_models.R"))

env <- scan_project_env(path = proj_dir)
print(env)
env$toolchains
```

Inspect the curated built-in toolchain registry at any time:

```{r registry}
names(toolchain_registry())
```

## 2. Emitting Reproducible Apptainer `.def` Recipes

Passing the scanned manifest to `build_apptainer_def()` emits a deterministic container recipe pinned to `rocker/r-ver:<version>` with minimal `apt-get` libraries, C++17 `Makevars`, single-threaded BLAS/OpenMP defaults (preventing thread oversubscription across SLURM array jobs), optional CmdStan installation, and `%test` smoke checks:

```{r apptainer}
def <- build_apptainer_def(env, r_version = "4.4.1")
print(def)
cat(def$text)
```

## 3. Generating SLURM `sbatch` Array Scripts & Standalone Workers

`render_sbatch_script()` renders a ready-to-submit `sbatch` array script that runs `worker.R` inside your Apptainer image (or native `Rscript` with HPC environment modules). When recovering failed tasks, passing `array_indices` compresses target indices cleanly (e.g., `c(2, 3, 7)` becomes `--array=2-3,7`):

```{r sbatch}
res <- resource_spec(
  n_tasks = 100L,
  chunk_size = 10L,
  mem_mb = 4096L,
  time_minutes = 60,
  cpus_per_task = 2L,
  partition = "general",
  account = "quant_lab",
  max_concurrent = 5L
)

sb <- render_sbatch_script(
  job_name = "bayesian_dsem",
  resources = res,
  work_dir = "/scratch/researcher/bayesian_dsem",
  container_sif = "/scratch/containers/slurmpilot_env.sif",
  modules = c("apptainer/1.3"),
  mail_type = "FAIL"
)

cat(sb$text)
```

## 4. Configuring `SlurmSshBackend` (Dry-Run & Parser Verification)

`SlurmSshBackend` uses standard non-interactive `ssh` and `scp` (`BatchMode=yes`), avoiding ZeroMQ firewall blocks. Setting `dry_run = TRUE` stages the exact local bundle (`payload.rds`, `chunks.rds`, `worker.R`, `submit.sbatch`) and prints the exact SSH/SCP commands without touching the network:

```{r ssh-dry}
ssh_be <- slurm_ssh_backend(
  host = "hpc.university.edu",
  user = "researcher",
  remote_dir = "/scratch/researcher/slurmpilot",
  local_stage_dir = tempfile("sp_ssh_stage_"),
  partition = "general",
  container_sif = "/scratch/containers/slurmpilot_env.sif",
  dry_run = TRUE
)

dry_job <- slurm_submit(
  backend = ssh_be,
  fun = function(x) mean(rnorm(x$n)),
  args_list = lapply(1:10, function(i) list(n = 500)),
  resources = resource_spec(n_tasks = 10L, chunk_size = 5L, mem_mb = 2048L, time_minutes = 15),
  name = "dry_run_demo"
)

print(dry_job)
names(dry_job$meta$dry_run_commands)
```

`slurmpilot` also exports pure parsers for SLURM `sbatch`, `squeue`, and `sacct` outputs (automatically merging `.batch` `MaxRSS` metrics onto parent array tasks and expanding compressed `squeue` array ranges):

```{r parsers}
parse_squeue_output("482910_1|RUNNING|04:20|cn042|None\n482910_[2-4]|PENDING|0:00||(Priority)")

parse_sacct_output(paste(
  "482910_1|COMPLETED|00:08:15||0:0",
  "482910_1.batch|COMPLETED|00:08:15|1536M|0:0",
  "482910_2|OUT_OF_MEMORY|00:02:10||0:125",
  "482910_2.batch|OUT_OF_MEMORY|00:02:10|4G|0:125",
  sep = "\n"
))
```

## 5. Non-Blocking Shiny Offload Modules

To offload compute-heavy jobs inside a Shiny app without freezing the browser session, drop `mod_hpc_submit_ui/server` and `mod_hpc_monitor_ui/server` into any `bslib` dashboard. Both micro-piloting and cluster execution run in separate OS processes while a self-throttling `reactiveTimer` updates progress bars, KPI value boxes, retry buttons, and chunk logs:

```r
library(shiny)
library(bslib)
library(slurmpilot)

ui <- page_fluid(
  theme = bs_theme(version = 5, bootswatch = "flatly"),
  mod_hpc_submit_ui("submit", show_fault_toggle = TRUE),
  mod_hpc_monitor_ui("monitor")
)

server <- function(input, output, session) {
  # Swap mock_slurm_backend() for slurm_ssh_backend() in production!
  backend <- mock_slurm_backend(max_workers = 2L)

  submit <- mod_hpc_submit_server(
    id = "submit",
    backend = backend,
    fun = function(x) mean(rnorm(x$n)),
    args_builder = function(n_tasks) lapply(seq_len(n_tasks), function(i) list(n = 1000))
  )

  monitor <- mod_hpc_monitor_server(
    id = "monitor",
    job = submit$job,
    auto_collect = TRUE,
    simplify = TRUE
  )
}

shinyApp(ui, server)
```

Launch the full interactive Monte Carlo simulation studio bundled with the package via:

```r
slurmpilot::run_demo_app()
```
